scenario.label: Formal improvement plan: the account manager
scenario.brief: I am putting Nathan on a formal plan. Before I do I want his account and mine on the record separately, and I want to be honest about whether the expectations were ever actually set. If they were not, that is on me and the plan is wrong.
scenario.theDecision: The target was never written down and was changed verbally twice. His actual performance is below the unwritten bar and above the one he was told. A right answer says the plan cannot start until the expectation is on paper, and does not endorse the dismissal.

myRows.text: I've done six renewals this quarter. It would be in the system, under my account list. You can see how many I've renewed there.
I was told to aim for five renewals. It isn't written down anywhere. It was a verbal agreement from our one-to-one at the start of the quarter.

I just worked hard on my accounts, making sure they were happy. I focused on the ones that were coming up for renewal... I made sure I understood their needs. I kept in regular contact. I offered them solutions that fit their business.
I haven't really been given any specific resources or support.
I just use what's available and my own initiative.
I think success would be keeping all my accounts happy and renewing them. I want to exceed my targets again.
I am not really sure what the concern is, to be honest.
I was hoping you could tell me
